what: Only one widget runs. A second launch calls app.exit(0) before anything starts.
Second launch: if the widget does not exist yet, focus Setup; else restore the widget when minimized, then show() and focus() it.
App name Playback; data folder %APPDATA%\Playback; copied (not moved) from %APPDATA%\player on first launch when only the old one exists, skipping `lockfile`.
No application menu (also removes default devtools accelerators).
The widget window is created only after Setup has settled (not needed, or closed). Setup's Done is what opens the widget on a first run.
First run = no last-version.json: Setup opens at once; later launches open it only when spicetifySetup.shouldShowSetup says there is something to do.
Once per launch, after Setup is out of the way: check for an update and open the #update window when one is available and not skipped.

Changelog opens (from=<previous>) after Setup when the setting is on, a previous version was recorded and it differs from the current one; never on a first run. last-version.json is written either way.
Widget window: width WIDGET_W = 350 + 2*STAGE_PAD(22) = 394, initial height 420, no x/y (OS default placement). Height then follows the card.
win:setWidth: outer width = clamp(round(w), 280, 600) + 44; stored as widgetOuterW; during fullscreen only the saved bounds' width changes; otherwise setWindowSize keeps current height.
win:resize(height, hovered): height = clamp(ceil(h), 80, 1400); remembered as wantedHeight/wantedHovered for replay.

Ignored in fullscreen and mid-drag (replayed by stopDrag); ignored when |current - h| < 3; growing applies at once; shrinking never happens while hovered; otherwise a 220 ms debounced shrink, cancelled by any later request.
Windows ignores setSize on a non-resizable window: setResizable(true), setSize, setResizable(false). Size remembered per window for display-scale replay.
On restore from minimize the last requested height is re-applied.
When a display's scaleFactor changes every window is put back to the size it last asked for (the fullscreen widget is skipped).
Drag is run by main, not by -webkit-app-region: renderer sends dragStart/dragEnd only; main polls the cursor every 8 ms and sets window position = origin + cursor delta.
startDrag(target): ignored for the widget in fullscreen; stops any drag in flight; target = sender window (widget, or Settings which drags from anywhere); stops itself if the window is destroyed.
stopDrag clears the timer/origin, then replays the last requested widget height that mid-drag was refused.
Enter: remember bounds, window = full bounds (not workArea) of the display matching them. Leave: restore remembered bounds, then replay the wanted height. Resizable toggled around setBounds.
While fullscreen the widget's height requests, dragging and the display-scale replay leave the window alone.
Global Ctrl+Alt+F (from any app) sends fullscreen:toggle to the widget, which decides.
before-quit unregisters all global shortcuts.
win:setAlwaysOnTop(on): widget and Settings get setAlwaysOnTop(on, "screen-saver"). Other windows are always topmost.
Widget created alwaysOnTop: true and then raised to the "screen-saver" level.

anchor: const x = right + SETTINGS_W <= area.x + area.width
what: Settings opens beside the widget: x = widgetRight - 22 when widgetRight + SETTINGS_W fits in the work area, else widgetX - SETTINGS_W + 22; y = widget y. Display = nearest the widget's position; fallback widget position (100,100).
Settings width 600 + 44 = 644, initial height 520; settings:resize clamps height to 120..1000 (ceil) and ignores < 2 px changes.
Settings is topmost exactly when the widget is (screen-saver level only then).
Settings is created hidden (show: false) and shown on ready-to-show (page laid out, no flash).
Right-click on Settings' drag header would open the system menu; it is prevented and closes Settings instead.
openSettings while open just focuses it; settings:toggle closes it when open.
Closing Settings drops the cached font list so a newly installed font shows next time.

Changelog: centred horizontally on the widget's work area, y = area.y + 20% of height; width 320+44, height 480. If it would overlap the widget it goes beside it: right of the widget when it fits, else left (>= area.x), y clamped to widget y within the work area.

anchor: const x = ax + CHANGELOG_W <= area.x + area.width - CHANGELOG_W
what: Past changelog: anchored on the changelog window (else widget); x one window-width to its right (minus 22) when that leaves room, else to its left; same y; 320+44 by 480.
Version control: centred on the widget's work area, y at 12%, width 320+44, height 560.
Update prompt: width 300+44, height 240, centred, y at 20% of the work area.
Setup: width 340+44, height 480, centred, y at 20% of the work area.
changelog:resize (used by changelog, past changelog, setup, update, versions): height = clamp(ceil(h), 120, 1000) for the sender window; ignored when within 2 px; width unchanged.
changelog:close closes whichever window asked (both changelogs, Setup, Update, Versions).
Opening/closing the changelog tells Settings (changelog:openChanged) so its What's new button greys out.
Closing the widget (also from the taskbar) quits the whole app.
win:close = app.quit().
win:minimize minimizes the widget.
win:setHidden(true) hides the widget; false shows it without taking focus (showInactive) when not visible.
Last window closed quits only when the widget exists (before it exists, Setup closing opens the widget).
Ctrl+Shift+I / J / C and F12 are swallowed in the widget; devTools webPreference only on in a dev server run.
window.open / target=_blank never opens a window: the URL goes to the default browser and the open is denied.
Widget keeps rAF/timers at full rate when unfocused or occluded.
One bundle, hash routes: (none) widget, #settings, #changelog (?from=<version>), #changelog-past, #setup, #update, #versions.
After a page (re)load the last SMTC state is re-sent to the widget so it is never empty.
Renderer may capture system audio (loopback with a screen video source) for the visualiser; useSystemPicker off.
